explanation: According to child development milestones studied in Home Economics, a newborn begins to show the first signs of head and body alignment (early posture awareness) at one month, when the baby can briefly lift the head while lying on the stomach. Options B (two months) and A (four months) represent later, more developed stages of postural control, while D (six months) is when a child can sit with support. The curriculum identifies one month as the starting point of postural development.
